text:
lucy: Heads-up — planning KMS setup for Redwood Private (VPC) control plane + dataplane. Questions about envelope pattern, RBAC, audit logs, and safe rotation. Anyone available?

omar: I can help. High-level idea: customer KEK in their KMS (AWS KMS CMK), use GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext for DEKs, store the DEK ciphertext blobs (no plaintext) in our tenant DB. Control plane holds only encrypted DEKs.

kevin: For RBAC we should use dedicated service principals per control-plane role and granular IAM conditions (sourceVpc, aws:CalledVia, aws:SourceIp) and map to k8s ServiceAccount via IRSA. Grant only GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext, Decrypt, and DescribeKey. No unbounded Encrypt/Sign perms.

tia: Quick rotation Q: do we rotate KEK or DEK? Proposed: rotate KEK (CMK) periodically; run a background rewrap job to re-encrypt existing DEK ciphertexts with the new KEK. Keep old KEK enabled for decrypt until rewrap completes. Staged rewrap avoids downtime.

omar: Rewrap strategy: incremental, tenant-by-tenant epochs. BatchRewrapJob should respect KMS DPS limits, use exponential backoff, and emit progress events. Use GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext + ReEncrypt? pattern to avoid exposing DEK plaintext in-app.

marco: Incident response notes: if KEK compromise suspected — immediate steps: 1) disable CMK (or rotate key material for non-AWS HSM) 2) promote a pre-configured fallback KEK 3) run recovery/rewrap from secure backup ciphertexts. We must document how to revoke grants and rotate service principals.

kevin: Audit logging: enable CloudTrail for all KMS key actions, stream to our logging pipeline (Splunk/Datadog). Add structured fields in our control-plane logs: tenant_id, request_id, node_id, and include KMS event IDs. Default retention 1y, with 7y for enterprise customers.

tia: On dataplane side: control-plane does KMS ops. Dataplane uses mTLS to talk to control-plane; never calls KMS directly. For on-prem/private deployments where customers host their own KMS endpoint, we need a KMS proxy/adapter with credentials stored in a customer-managed KMS secret and strict network ACLs.

omar: Cross-account grants: prefer CreateGrant with RetireGrant enabled and use grant tokens for bootstrap handoffs. Avoid long-lived cross-account key policies unless absolutely required. Grants are auditable via CloudTrail events (CreateGrant/RetireGrant).

lucy: RBAC change flow suggestion: require a PR template when updating key policies or IAM roles, run a small canary, and add post-change audit checks (smoke test that does GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext + Decrypt on a test tenant).

marco: Putting some playbook commands here for ops runbook, e.g.
```bash
# grant to controlplane role for tenant KEK
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane --operations GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-ops
```

kevin: Implementation note: cache DEKs in memory for <30s and zero them after use, never persist plaintext. Use HSM-backed KMS for KEK ops and enforce TLS 1.2+.

lucy: Action items: omar to draft rewrap job design, kevin to update IAM/IRSA templates, tia to add CI smoke-tests, marco to write incident KB. I'll draft RBAC PR template and runbook. :thumbsup:

aws-kms-bot: [info] KMS policy change detected for alias/tenant-kev by lucy@redwood — see CloudTrail event id=0xabc123

omar: I'll post a short design doc later: https://redwood.internal/docs/kms-priv-vpc-envelope-design

lucy: thanks all — syncing with compliance on retention requirements tomorrow.
